It describes her waters flowing from high Hukairya to the sea Vouru-kasha, stirring its gulfs, having many tributaries and outlets, and dividing toward the seven Karshvars. It calls the saints' Fravashis near, excludes evildoers from the good waters, asks the waters to remain in place while the priest offers, and insists that offerings be made with proper ritual words as taught and as Ahura Mazda showed to Zarathustra.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Ardvi Sura Anahita is described as efficacious against the Daevas, devoted to Ahura's lore, holy, worshipped with sacrifice, and beneficial to living things, herds, settlements, wealth, and the Province.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Ardvi Sura Anahita is said to purify male seed, sanctify women's wombs for birth, make women fortunate in labour, and bring a regular timely flow of milk.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Ardvi Sura Anahita is described as a great water-volume, sounding or famed from afar, equal in bulk to all waters flowing on earth, and flowing from high Hukairya to the sea Vouru-kasha.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"When Ardvi Sura Anahita rushes or plunges foaming into Vouru-kasha, its gulfs and middle are stirred; she is described as having a thousand tributaries and a thousand between good and malicious genii; a Magical Tree; the Rock of Two-holes opened by secret voice-knowledge; enormous monsters; a huge River Tortoise mistaken for an island; and a Fiery Serpent.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The passage says the Zulus have nursery tales and that women are the depositaries of these tales.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The passage presents the tales as potentially showing points of contact between the Zulus and other peoples and resemblances to other traditional tales.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The first tale in the series is described as the travels and adventures of Uthlakanyana, called a kind of Tom Thumb and Giant Killer.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Uthlakanyana is described as not a common man, but a cunning, malicious dwarf with gulp.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Uzwanide, also called Long-toe, is described as an ogress and mighty magician capable of rising from a succession of deaths.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Animals including leopard, hare, iguana, doves, swallows, pigeons, and mice are said to talk freely and interact with powers.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The passage says all the tales allude more or less distinctly to magic and to a contest between good and malicious children.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Members of the marriage company petition the Isikgukqumadevu, blame Untombinde for bringing An editorial note compares the tale with South African elephant-as-king traditions and especially a Basuto Little Hare tale involving a fabulous animal, a woman who drinks a lake dry, an ostrich who restores the water, and a hare who shifts blame to a jerboa.
